newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says plans Griffin oil closing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says plans Griffin oil closing.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said it plans to halt crude production at the Griffin offshore oil field offshore Western Australia later on Monday due to an approaching cyclone.

Given the current predictions for the path of cyclone Rachel, which is barelling down the coastal region of Western Australia, the Griffin production platform would probably disconnect from its mooring early on Tuesday and head for calmer seas, the spokesman said.
"It looks like it's coming our way," a BHP spokesman said.

The platform, which was producing about 70,000 barrels of crude a day, was disconnected from its mooring offshore Western Australia last Sunday to escape the path of the previous cyclone Phil, which has since dissipated, and only reconnected last Friday, he said.
"We never really had a chance to get up to speed on production," the spokesman said.

At 0400 GMT (midday local), cyclone Rachel was estimated to be 200 km west of the coastal town of Broome and 300 km northeast of Port Hedland, traveling west-southwest at 15 km an hour, the Bureau of Meteorology said.
BHP would assess weather conditions on Tuesday morning before making a final decision whether to disconnect the platofrm from its mooring, the spokesman said.
Expectations are for Rachel to intensify into a category three cyclone Monday evening with winds between 170 and 224 km an hour, the bureau said.
Rachel is currently rated a category two cyclone, meaning it carries winds between 125 and 169 km an hour
BHP holds a 45-percent interest in the Griffin oil project and is the operator. Mobil Corp holds 35 percent and Inpex Alpha Ltd owns the remaining 20 percent.
Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Monday it plans to halt production of crude oil at the Cossack Pioneer oil rig at around 1000 GMT (six p.m. local time) on Monday due to the cyclone.
The Cossack Pioneer pumps crude oil and gas from the Wanaea and Cossack fields on the North West Shelf of the Indian Ocean.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf project are units of BHP, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside
